title: GPOM: the door and the proof
about: This page holds three combined drafts for the bridge between the kill bots' stand-down and Maddie on the step, plus all ten writers' versions ranked underneath. Nothing in the cut, the script or the voices has changed yet.

dialogues.label: The door and the proof
dialogues.where: Between scene A's stand-down and scene C's step
dialogues.target: spoken 20 s or less; whole bridge about 35 s including a wordless ~8 s replay

drafts.name: 1F + the boom (heard, not seen)
drafts.bet: Kai, 2 Nov: we hear the explosion. After the film, Maddie blows up the kill bot off screen; the bunker hears it, Derek sees the smoking wreck through the periscope, then Maddie leaves. Proof they witnessed themselves.

lines.line: Hey, humans! Sorry about the intrusion.

lines.who: Maddie (same breath, quick, quieter: the aside)
lines.line: [mumbled] ...And everything else.
We didn't think there were any of you left. [pause] But now we've found you... there might be a way we could fix this mess.

lines.who: Old lady (INSIDE, seen, shouting at the door)
lines.line: Are you literally joking?

lines.who: Old lady (OUTSIDE on Maddie: the same shout, muffled through the steel)
lines.line: You killed everybody!
Yeah. [pause] That's... that's fair.
How can we win your trust?
Look. We really do understand this has gone the worst way for everybody. [pause] I'll leave you a film to watch. It's our best go at proving it.

[Room shot BP1-e-b, the TV in the distance under the megaphone. On it (post): wa-05, the kill bot's own eyes racing at THEIR door, red KILL MODE; it brakes; the HUD flips to NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE (hud.py peace state, same as scene A); they file away. The screen light goes red to green on the backs of their heads.]
Oh, and... [beat] thought you'd want to hear this bit for yourselves.
[A deep, muffled BOOM through the earth. The bulb under the megaphone swings; dust sifts down from the vault onto upturned faces.]

[Derek at the periscope (BP2-d-b): he presses his eye to it. Cut to what he sees (BP3-e-a): the kill bot a burnt-out wreck, turret blown off, a thread of smoke, a crow landing on it; Maddie waiting near-left, beacon lit.]

lines.who: Maddie (tannoy, through the periscope view; her beacon pulses)
lines.line: Right. I'll come back tomorrow.
[Through the periscope: Maddie trundles away out of the circle. Derek steps back from the eyepiece.]

lines.who: Sandra (to the old lady, not taking her eyes off the screen)
lines.line: If there's a way to fix this, I'd love to take it. It fucking sucks living in this bunker. [beat] With grumpy Derek.
[off] Oi.

lines.who: Old lady (not agreeing; stating a fact, flat)
lines.line: Well. [pause] I don't know. [pause] We do have the dwindling food supply problem. [long pause] Perhaps we should vote.
The next day.
[Into C as cut: Maddie on the step, the hundred file out behind her.]

notes: Your ruling: the explosion is heard, never seen.
Maddie's 'I'll come back tomorrow' moves after the boom, so she leaves after the proof, seen going through the periscope.
New line (mine, change freely): "Oh, and... thought you'd want to hear this bit for yourselves."
Unchanged after it: Sandra, Derek's 'Oi', the old lady's food line, 'Perhaps we should vote.', card 'The next day.'

drafts.name: 1D with your notes
drafts.bet: 1D as you noted it: one 'grumpy', an old lady who doesn't agree so much as admit a fact, no vote shown at all. The film is the open job (see the film options in Claude's read).

[THE FILM, about 14 s, no words. F1: the kill bot's own eyes racing at THEIR door (their sign, the moss on the blast doors, the tannoy horn, Maddie in shot), timestamped twenty minutes ago; someone mouths 'that's us'. F2: on the same HUD, KILL MODE, then the objective line rewrites: NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE; the bots turn and file away; a hundred faces lit by it. F3, after the film: Derek climbs to the old periscope and looks out: the track marks lead away, and out in the field a kill bot sits powered down, a bird landing on it.]

notes: L10: 'grumpy' once.
L12: your wording, flat and reluctant: it's a fact she admits, not a yes.
L13: no hands, nothing about the vote; straight from 'Perhaps we should vote.' to the card 'The next day.' and Maddie leading them out.
Derek's 'Oi.' kept (cut it if you like).
Line 9, the film: four options in Claude's read at the top.
PICKED 2026-11-02 (Kai: 'I think we've got a script'). Film = F1 then F2 then F3; overlay NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE; card 'The next day.'

drafts.name: Kai's setup: watch this, I'll come back tomorrow
drafts.bet: No one is persuaded on screen. Maddie apologises, takes the shouting, leaves them a film and goes. The humans have their own reasons (the bunker, Derek, the food), we see the debate start, and the next day answers it.

notes: Your words throughout; only joins tidied. Spoken ~34 s plus an 8 s film and a card: about 48 s, longer than the 35 s target, but it is a real scene with a turn, not a link.
'Sandra... grumpy, grumpy Derek' pays off in D: 'Does this mean I get to hang out with non-grumpy Derek?'
'Derek: Oi.' is mine (one syllable of air); cut it if you like.
The decision is assumed, never said: hands going up, then the next day.
HUD: the film shows NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE; scene A currently says STAND DOWN. Either the film is a re-captioned replay, or A gets the same text so the audience recognises it.

drafts.name: 1D, tightest
drafts.bet: The same setup at the bone: if 1D drags, these are the cuts.

lines.line: Hey, humans! Sorry about the intrusion. [mumbled] ...And everything else.
We didn't think there were any of you left. But now we've found you, there might be a way we could fix this mess.

lines.who: Old lady (INSIDE seen, then OUTSIDE muffled)
lines.line: Are you literally joking? [cut outside, muffled] You killed everybody!
Yeah. That's fair. [pause] How can we win your trust?
I'll leave you a film. Our best go at proving it. I'll come back tomorrow.
[Kill bot's eyes: KILL MODE; brake; NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE. Faces lit by it.]
If there's a way to fix this, I'll take it. It fucking sucks in this bunker. With grumpy Derek.
And we're running out of food. [pause] Let's vote.

notes: Cuts from 1D: 'We really do understand this has gone the worst way for everybody', 'Oi', the hands going up, one 'grumpy'.
Risk: without 'We really do understand...' the apology is only the joke plus 'That's fair'.

drafts.name: The lady sets the terms
drafts.bet: Real resistance beats a clever mechanism: the humans only open the door because the old lady demands to see, so the proof is extracted, not sold, and Maddie never pitches.

lines.line: Oh, hello, humans. Sorry about the intrusion.
And, you know. All of it.

lines.who: Old lady (INSIDE, seen, existing lip-sync take)
lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved.

lines.who: Old lady (OUTSIDE shot of Maddie, muffled through the steel)
lines.line: There's no way we're going anywhere with you. You killed everybody.
I don't blame you. I can see how it looks.
We've got a way we might be able to fix this. How could I win your trust?

lines.who: Old lady (INSIDE, up at the spyhole, clear again)
lines.line: Something came to our door. Show me.

[Bunker's dead CCTV monitors flicker on one by one: red KILL MODE racing at this very door, brake, flip to green STAND DOWN, filing away. Cut to a hundred faces lit by it, Sandra's hand over her mouth, Derek silent for once. Hold on the old lady's glasses holding two green rectangles.]
Derek. The bolts.
[Bolts. The door grinds open on daylight. Hand to C: Maddie on the step.]

notes: Spoken total 19.8 s. If it runs long, cut 'And, you know. All of it.' (-1.5 s) first.
Dropped Kai's 'Yeah,' and 'The thing is,' for time; restore 'Yeah,' as a one-word lead-in if budget allows.
Risk: 'Show me' can read as Maddie being led; play her relieved. Needs a low thump or rumble in scene A so 'Something came to our door' is earned.
Risk: needs one new plate of the CCTV bank and a stand-down insert matching A's angle.
Maddie says nothing during or after the replay; she never explains the footage.

drafts.name: Silence is the yes
drafts.bet: The tightest honest version: Maddie concedes and asks, nobody answers in words, and the decision is a hand on a wheel, so the faces going red then green carry everything.

lines.line: Oh, hello, humans. Sorry about the intrusion.
My boss is ever so sorry. About all of it.

lines.who: Old lady (INSIDE, seen, not raising her voice)
lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved.

lines.who: Old lady (OUTSIDE, muffled, door in frame)
lines.line: There's no way we're going anywhere with you. You killed everybody.
I don't blame you. I can see how it looks.
We've got a way we might be able to fix this.
How could I win your trust?
[Tannoy hiss left open. No answer. The fan. Cut inside: the lady looks at the dark monitors.]
[Old CCTV monitors come up by themselves; the replay seen mostly as red then green light on faces and in the old lady's glasses, one money-shot glimpse of STAND DOWN. Her hand goes to the wheel.]
[Bolts one at a time; door grinds open on daylight. Hand to C.]

notes: Spoken 18.0 s, protected lines all verbatim, plus one new line ('My boss is ever so sorry').
'My boss' hands the old lady her hook for 'Your boss killed everyone', so the refusal has a cause on screen.
Cut from every other shape: any lady rebuttal, any Sandra/Derek gag, any Maddie narration over the replay.
Risk: the humans cave in about 15 s with no spoken turn; the faces and the wheel must be sold by the performance and sound (tannoy hiss, the row going dead).
Risk: replay fatigue, the audience just saw the stand-down; show it from the humans' side, with S6 only for the money shot.
Risk: the closest to 'no dialogue'; Kai asked for 'a bit'.

drafts.name: Laugh, then grief
drafts.bet: The tannoy cutting the toilet-seat row dead gets the laugh Kai loved, and the old lady is the one person not laughing, so the refusal hits harder for the clowning round it.

lines.line: [Inside, dim: Sandra and Derek mid-row, hushed. A tannoy SQUEAL cuts them dead; a hundred heads turn to the door.]
Oh, hello, humans. Sorry about the intrusion.
Is that about the seat?
And the rest of it. Sorry.
Your boss killed everyone we ever loved.
There's no way we're going anywhere with you. You killed everybody.
I don't blame you. I can see how it looks.
We've got a way we might be able to fix this. How could I win your trust?
[Dead CCTV monitors flicker up; red KILL MODE at this very door, brake, green STAND DOWN, filing away. A hundred faces lit by it; Sandra's mouth open mid-row, Derek has stopped chewing.]

lines.who: Old lady (not looking away from the screen)
lines.line: Derek. Door.
[Wheel turns, bolts, door grinds open onto daylight. Hand to C.]

notes: Spoken 19.0 s.
Giving 'Derek. Door.' to the old lady (not Sandra) keeps the decision hers; the draft-1 shape had Sandra say it, which undercuts the resistance.

Risk: the seat gag sours the apology if the room is still laughing at 'And the rest of it. Sorry.'; the cheer must slip on that line. It also depends on the audience remembering the seat from scene A.
Risk: the half-and-half needs the seen and muffled voice to be clearly the same woman.
Dropped 'Yeah,' and 'The thing is,' for time.

ranking.verdict: Strongest resistance: the lady turns Maddie's open question into a condition ('Show me'), so the decision is the humans' and the replay is an answer, not a pitch. Fails: sits right at the 20 s ceiling, 'Something came to our door' needs scene A to plant it, and 'Show me' half-states the mechanism.

Best craft logic (concede first, ask, restraint shown not claimed) and 'my boss' gives the refusal a cause. Fails: the lady's two refusal lines say nearly the same thing, the bridge runs ~36 s, and the apology rides on a volume drop.

Cleanest and nearest to Kai's brief; the faces make the decision. Fails: no spoken turn at all after the question, so the cave-in risks feeling sudden, and nine camera setups is a lot to shoot for a short bridge.

Elegant: the replay is only light on faces and glasses, so it is cheap and not a repeat of scene A. Fails: nobody inside concedes anything, so the choice must live in a glasses reflection; 'Everything' is thin.
On target, nothing wasted. Fails: seven seconds of Maddie in a row is a run-up; 'Everything.' can read flip; no comic air, so the tannoy squeal has to earn all of it.
Humans work out the proof for themselves, which is persuasive. Fails: invents a still-taping door camera that must be planted, and removes Maddie from the replay, against Kai's 'Maddie replays it'.
Door-as-instrument is the right sound idea (adopted in every draft). Fails: 'Right. Have a look at this, then.' explains the move; the proof then costs Maddie a line the others do without.

The thump-the-camera idea is a good joke and the tread marks are a nice outside proof. Fails: a working five-year-old camera is a plausibility cheat, 'give it a thump' can read flippant after the grief, and it needs a new monochrome asset.
The tannoy-cutting-a-row gag is the one Kai loved. Fails as a whole: the seat joke risks souring the apology, and Sandra deciding ('Derek. Door.') undercuts the old lady; kept only as the gag in 1C.
Fails: whispered overlapping crowd lines turn to mush in the mix, the 1 s beats are cuttable without loss, and a collective voice scene C will not carry through.

questions.text: The film (your note: the most important wordless beat): which of F1-F4, or which combination? My pick: F1 + F3 (their own door on the recording, then they check it with their own eyes).

Overlay text: just NEW OBJECTIVE: SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE, or the old objective struck through first (ELIMINATE ORGANIC SIGNAL → SUSTAIN ORGANIC LIFE)? And should scene A's stand-down carry the same words?
Card: 'The next day.' or 'The next morning.'?
